content.text:
Silhouette: Horizontal red fox frame carried on two hind legs, barn owl wings in place of the forelegs. Host frame: the red fox sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature combining a red fox and a barn owl. The head is that of the red fox, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: red fox body and legs with its own dense fur on the face, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs and tail; plain coat with no stripes or spots. From the barn owl, as parts and materials on the red fox's own body: broad wings of layered flight feathers in place of the forelegs, standing on two hind legs, wings sized for flight; layered contour feathers in its own colors grown from the skin as the red fox's own covering over the shoulders and neck, replacing the red fox's dense fur there and conforming to the red fox's body, sized to the red fox's body and following its contours. Every covered part keeps the red fox's own length and shape; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, while the face, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs and tail keep the red fox's own dense fur; deep keel and heavy flight chest. The covering follows the body's own shape. Bilaterally symmetrical, with recognizable limbs and visible sense organs. Habitat cue (desert): larger ears and longer tail for shedding heat. Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing hybrid creature image**
I'm planning a single creature that merges a red fox body on two hind legs with barn owl wings instead of forelegs, keeping the fox head fully visible with clear eyes and dense, plain fur.
**Composing natural history illustration**
I'm drafting a side three-quarter, full-body illustration of a bipedal red fox with wings instead of forelegs, feathered shoulders and neck, deep keel chest, larger ears and longer tail, set on a plain light background with natural lighting and soft shadow.
**Refining creature illustration pose**
I'm adjusting the creature to stand upright on two hind legs, replace the forelegs with wings, and use a side three-quarter view for the new generation.
